after.condition: Shared input is a text string or an ordered array of messages, function calls, custom tool calls and outputs. Match each tool output to its call with call_id. Developer/system messages accept input text only; system messages are treated as developer messages. Assistant messages accept output text or refusals. Tool outputs accept text and images. Files, audio and item references are unsupported.

Images may use inline base64 data URLs or publicly accessible HTTP/HTTPS URLs, not file_id. User messages may combine input_text and input_image. Predicate, choice and score question instructions may be a nonempty array of input_text/input_image parts without a message wrapper or role; question images share the request's image limits with shared input.

input_json content parts carry a JSON object or array in data and are supported only in user-message content. JSON keys inside data do not create messages or fetch images; JSON input does not change the typed-answer response format.

At most four cache breakpoints may be written per request. Matching considers the latest 80 conversation breakpoints without a content-block lookback limit. ttl defaults to 30m, currently its only supported value. These SDK constraints are recorded only for native gpt-6-luna Decisions, not inherited by other model families or Copilot.

Cache reuse requires an identical shared-input prefix of at least 1,024 tokens; questions and question images are outside that prefix. An implicit breakpoint at the end of shared input is the default. prompt_cache_key partitions reuse; prompt_cache_breakpoint on shared text/image parts marks explicit boundaries. prompt_cache_options.mode=explicit disables the implicit boundary; without marked boundaries explicit mode does not cache. Breakpoints are unsupported in question instructions. Cache-read and cache-write token counts are already included in usage.input_tokens.

proposal.summary: Add the documented 2-10 score-level constraint, role/tool-call input restrictions, user-only JSON parts, hosted/inline image and question-image constraints, and shared-prefix prompt-cache controls (1024-token minimum, question exclusion, explicit boundaries, usage accounting, four writes, 80-breakpoint matching and 30m TTL). Record captured guide/SDK hashes and retrieval times only on changed feature facts. Preserve existing exact model/protocol support and all Copilot authentication, lifecycle and availability facts. Copilot tariff identity gaps and unfetched lifecycle announcements remain incomplete, not evidence of compatibility or retirement.

evidence.quote: Send requests to POST /v1/decisions using gpt-6-luna , the only currently supported model.
questions: Ask 1–400 questions about the input. Each question can be a predicate, choice, or score. Answers come back in the same order.
A score question evaluates an input against 2–10 ordered levels .
input Shared evidence for the questions: a text string or an ordered array of messages, tool calls, and tool outputs.

Pass conversation history in input to evaluate a request in context. Include messages and any function or custom tool calls and outputs in order. Match each tool output to its call with call_id . The supported content depends on the message role or item type: Input item Supported content User message Text, images, and JSON Developer or system message Input text only; system messages are treated as developer messages Assistant message Output text or refusals Function or custom tool output Text and images, associated with a matching tool call
Files, audio, and item references aren’t supported.

Use an input_json content part to pass structured evidence without first converting it to a string. Put the JSON object or array in data , alongside any text or image parts in a user message. Within message content, input_json is supported only for the user role.

JSON keys such as role or image_url inside data are ordinary data: they don’t create messages or fetch images. The answer still uses the selected question type; JSON input doesn’t change the response format.

Provide images as inline base64 data URLs or publicly accessible HTTP or HTTPS URLs. This endpoint doesn’t support file_id inputs. Combine input_text and input_image parts in a user message to evaluate images together with instructions or other context.

To give each question a different image, set its instructions to a nonempty array of input_text and input_image parts. This works for predicate, choice, and score questions. Text-only instructions can remain a string.
Supply content parts directly in instructions , without a message wrapper or role . Question images share the request’s image limits with images in input .

Prompt caching lets repeated requests reuse a matching prefix of shared input and receive discounted cache-read pricing. For example, keep a reference document or image in input and change the questions for each request. Content in questions , including question-specific images, is outside the reusable prefix. By default, Decisions places an implicit cache breakpoint at the end of shared input . Existing requests can benefit without changing their request body. The reusable prefix must contain at least 1,024 tokens; question content doesn’t count toward this threshold. Keep the prefix identical across requests to allow reuse. Use prompt_cache_key to partition cache reuse by a caller-provided key. For control over the boundary, add prompt_cache_breakpoint: {"mode": "explicit"} to text or image content parts in shared input . Set prompt_cache_options.mode to "explicit" to use only marked boundaries. In explicit mode, a request with no marked boundaries doesn’t use prompt caching. Breakpoints aren’t supported in question instructions. Check usage.input_tokens_details.cached_tokens for cache reads and usage.input_tokens_details.cache_write_tokens for cache writes. Both counts are included in usage.input_tokens ; don’t add them to that total.

Each request can write up to four breakpoints. For cache matching, OpenAI considers up to the latest 80 breakpoints in the conversation, without a content-block lookback limit. Set `mode` to `explicit` to disable the implicit breakpoint. The `ttl` defaults to `30m`, which is currently the only supported value.
